sections.body: The AI Economist covers ten areas where machine learning, large language models, and automated data pipelines meet economic measurement and investment practice. In forecasting, models now blend traditional econometrics with high-frequency data, text from central bank statements, and nowcasting techniques to estimate activity before official statistics arrive. In trading, AI systems parse order books, news, and filings to generate signals, size positions, and manage execution, though many production systems remain hybrid with human oversight. In private equity and credit, models help screen deals, extract terms from contracts, and flag borrower stress using documents and payment data. This site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which gives a concrete view of how public markets price the theme. The work is not a single product but a set of methods applied across forecasting, allocation, risk, and compliance.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are genuinely solved at scale, such as parsing earnings calls, classifying news sentiment, detecting anomalies in transaction data, and running backtests on well-defined signals. Other tasks remain hard, including stable macroeconomic forecasting during regime shifts, causal inference from observational data, and explaining why a deep model made a particular trade. Data quality, survivorship bias, look-ahead bias, and non-stationarity are persistent limits, and a model that works in one market regime may fail in another. Regulation and fiduciary duties add another layer, because an automated recommendation can create liability even when the model is statistically sound. The site tracks 149 active AI lawsuits and 222 compliance and regulation pages, which shows that legal and governance questions are now part of the economics beat. Honest limits include limited transparency, unclear accountability, and the difficulty of validating models against rare events.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader can start with Macroeconomic Econometrics for the statistical foundations of forecasting and nowcasting, then move to Quantitative Trading for signal generation, execution, and backtesting. Private Equity and Deal Sourcing covers how AI screens companies and supports diligence, drawing on the site's 393 merger and acquisition filings. Fixed Income and Credit Risk focuses on default prediction, spread analysis, and loan monitoring, while Portfolio Construction connects those inputs to allocation, risk budgeting, and rebalancing. Reading the Market's Language examines sentiment, narrative, and textual signals from filings and news, and Alternative Data explains the use of satellite, card, web, and other non-traditional sources. Agent Workflows in Finance looks at multi-step automation for research, reporting, and operations, and Crypto Markets and Decentralised Finance applies similar methods to on-chain data, tokens, and decentralised protocols. Governance and Fiduciary Risk ties the section together by covering oversight, disclosure, and legal exposure, which is where the site's 149 active AI lawsuits and 222 compliance and regulation pages become relevant.
